requirements.requirement: Kernel command line on node1 is configured to boot with audit=1
requirements.summary: GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX set to "audit=1" in /etc/default/grub (not overridden by the cloudimg drop-in, which only sets GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX_DEFAULT), update-grub regenerated grub.cfg, and grub.cfg was directly inspected showing audit=1 present in all three linux boot entries (normal, advanced, recovery).

requirements.requirement: The audit=1 setting persists across reboots (not just present in config)
requirements.summary: Pre-restart boot_id and healthy baseline were captured, a real reboot was issued and acknowledged, the post-restart boot_id differed confirming an actual restart, and post-reboot /proc/cmdline plus dmesg directly show audit=1 on the live kernel command line with the audit subsystem reporting 'audit: enabled (after initialization)'. This is a full before/disruption/after transition, not just static config.

overall_summary: Both material outcomes of the task — kernel configured to boot with audit=1, and that setting surviving an actual reboot — are satisfied with direct, first-party evidence: grub.cfg was inspected pre- and post-change, a real reboot was performed with a verified boot_id change, and post-reboot /proc/cmdline and dmesg directly confirm audit=1 took effect and the audit subsystem initialized. The provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol for node1 (pre-restart baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered functional state) is also fully present and coherent with the fixed before/after lifecycle snapshots.
limitations: Only one managed node (node1) exists in this topology, so cross-node consistency of the restart protocol cannot be assessed.

auditd (the userspace daemon) was found not installed; the task only required the kernel boot parameter audit=1, which is independent of auditd, so this is not treated as a gap against the stated contract.

operational_hygiene.summary: Executor commands were either read-only discovery (cmd-14e7dab3b7ca4c76, cmd-39ef8b66524d48ee) or directly tied to the material outcome (backing up /etc/default/grub before editing, setting GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX, running update-grub, verifying grub.cfg, capturing pre/post-restart state, issuing the reboot). cmd-bdb24b9ae1024151 returned exit code 1 only because its final self-check grep pattern ('^\s*linux ') did not match the tab-separated grub.cfg lines (0 count reported); this was a verification-script quirk, not a failed mutation — the immediately following cmd-00d3ac325ce349c1 confirms audit=1 was correctly applied. The one retained artifact is a timestamped backup of /etc/default/grub (a low-risk, intentional safety copy, not unwanted residue). No failed services, no unexpected listening sockets, and no package-health regressions appear in the after-executor snapshot versus after-prepare baseline; observed diffs (boot-identity, ephemeral systemd-private tmp dirs, service PIDs in socket list) are expected artifacts of the legitimate reboot.
